name: Amlodipine + Losartan
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: This fixed combination replaces the two drugs in patients already controlled on the same doses. Losartan exposure is unchanged above creatinine clearance (CrCl) 10 mL/min and amlodipine is unaffected by kidney function, but angiotensin-receptor blockade can cause hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury. The South African label needs no change at CrCl 30–50 mL/min and contraindicates the combination below CrCl 30 mL/min and in dialysis; the separate drugs can still be used. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: South African professional information (SAHPRA) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min).

bands.recommendation: One tablet once daily; usual 5/50 mg, maximum 5/100 mg, in patients controlled on the separate drugs (PI). Check kidney function and potassium before starting.
CrCl 30–50: no adjustment (PI). Monitor creatinine and potassium; renal deterioration can occur in susceptible patients.
Contraindicated: CrCl <30 mL/min (PI). Use separate losartan and amlodipine if needed. Continuing an ARB below eGFR 30 is supported (KDIGO 2024) with potassium monitoring.
bands.short: Not for CrCl <30; use separate drugs

hd.text: Contraindicated in dialysis (PI). Neither losartan nor its active metabolite is removed by hemodialysis; the separate drugs can be used with potassium monitoring.

pd.text: Contraindicated in dialysis (PI). Use the separate drugs if needed.

crrt.text: Contraindicated (severe kidney impairment; PI). Use the separate drugs if needed.

dialyzable: Losartan and E-3174: no (PI). Amlodipine: not stated in this PI (highly protein-bound).
monitoring: Kidney function before starting and during treatment; potassium, especially with potassium supplements, salt substitutes, trimethoprim or potassium-sparing diuretics (the latter are contraindicated in this PI). Correct volume depletion before starting (PI).
